supporting_observations.claim: The account was created at 13:45:01 UTC, later than the alert's approximate 13:42 time.
The account name follows the stated temporary-account naming pattern, and the creation event identifies help-desk user lena.ward as the actor.
The recorded group addition for v.rwong is to Vendors, matching the stated practice for temporary accounts; the provided records show no administrator-group addition.
The creation event's subject logon ID matches lena.ward's network logon on DC-SUN-01 shortly beforehand, consistent with the recorded actor attribution.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not establish whether the account creation was requested or approved.
The records show a Vendors group addition, but do not establish the account's complete or subsequent group memberships.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether lena.ward's credentials or session were compromised.
claims_not_established: Whether v.rwong corresponds to a real, authorized vendor or has an appropriate expiration date.
Whether the account received privileges or access not represented in the supplied records.
Whether the activity was performed by lena.ward personally.
additional_evidence_needed: For a separate investigation, review the DC-SUN-01 and FILE-SUN-01 RDP session activity and determine whether lena.ward's access was authorized.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: lena.ward initiated RDP sessions to DC-SUN-01 and FILE-SUN-01, although the inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-IDOYLE-01; the records also show dsa.msc launched with high integrity on WS-LWARD-01. These observations do not by themselves establish that the account creation was malicious. (T258-00077, T258-00079, T258-00080, T258-00094, T258-00099, T258-00100, T258-00107, T258-00108, T258-00110)
